item.name: Domain Ramp Aggro
item.description: Focus on playing multiple varied basic lands and creatures with Domain payoffs. Use ramp spells (like those that generate different colored mana) to quickly reach five unique basic land types, then attack aggressively to trigger Nael's combat damage condition and draw cards.

example_cards.name: Domain Payoff Creature
example_cards.reason: This creature acts as the repeatable threat generator and engine trigger. It must be resilient enough to attack multiple times, dealing consistent combat damage to maintain Nael’s card draw loop against opponents.

example_cards.name: Card Draw/Utility Spell
example_cards.reason: A powerful support piece that either draws cards independently or provides crucial recursive utility (e.g., tutoring for necessary basic lands or generating extra board-wide value) to keep the engine running even if combat is temporarily stalled.

priorities.category: Mana Fixing and Basic Land Diversity
priorities.reason: This is the single most critical element. The core loop requires controlling five distinct basic land types (Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, Forest) to activate Nael's strongest draw condition.
The engine only triggers on combat damage. The deck needs reliable, resilient creatures that can maintain pressure and ensure repeated attacks, even if the board state is contested.

Given Nael's ability to look at the top of the library, having utility or recursive cards (like artifact tutors or land fetchers) ensures that even if the optimal basic lands are depleted, alternatives can maintain board presence.

strengths: The exponential card advantage engine: Achieving five basic land types allows Nael to draw a card every time he successfully deals combat damage, creating an infinite loop of resource generation.

Efficient board acceleration via Domain: By requiring only the *type* of basic land (not owning them all) and leveraging ramp spells, the deck can quickly reach the necessary 5/5 configuration without relying solely on expensive fetch lands or dedicated mana rocks.

Low-risk threat generation: The strategy relies heavily on aggressively attacking with creatures that benefit from Domain payoffs, meaning threats are generated through synergy rather than high individual costs.

Flexible land base: Because only the basic *type* matters for Nael's trigger condition, the deck can incorporate diverse non-basic lands (e.g., utility or filtering lands) without impeding the primary goal.
weaknesses: Vulnerability to targeted board wipes: Mass damage spells that clear the battlefield before combat will halt the draw engine entirely.
Dependence on early ramp and land fixing: If the opponent can remove vital basic land types or delay reaching 5 unique basic types, Nael's primary payoff is severely curtailed.

Reliance on attacking: The entire strategy hinges on connecting with combat damage. Opponents who control board-wipes that prevent creatures from attacking (e.g., removal targeting only attackers) can stall the engine.
Susceptibility to counterspells: Key ramp or land-fixing spells must be cast safely, as being countered before they resolve delays reaching 5 basic types.

win_conditions.description: The primary win condition is attrition. By leveraging Nael's ability to draw cards repeatedly through combat damage triggers, the deck out-resources opponents, building a massive board presence and overwhelming them with combat damage before they can mount a defense.
win_conditions.name: Overwhelming Aggro Combat Damage

weaknesses: The entire strategy is heavily reliant on creatures being able to successfully engage in combat; if the board stalls or threats are removed before they can attack, the primary draw engine halts.
